cases.statement: Two people in the batch papers: the Paprocka 2024 proband (male infant, heterozygous, neonatal-onset course, died at 4 months) and a previously published patient from Mura et al. 2021 (PMID 34865968, not in the batch) known only from summary sentences and a review table. 41443241 Table 3 re-lists both (Paprocka column and Mura column), so its two rows are very probably the same two people.

people.label: patient (proband)
people.key_phenotypes: drug-resistant seizures from the first weeks of life; hydrocephalus with raised intracranial pressure needing a ventriculoperitoneal shunt; frontally predominant white-matter signal change with basal ganglia enhancement on MRI; severe hyponatremia; death at 4 months

quotes.quote: In proband’s sample missense heterozygous variant in the GFAP gene (NM_002055.5:c.1187C>T, p.(Thr396Ile))
We studied the proband’s sample, along with his healthy parents and sister
A 6-week-old infant was admitted to the Pediatric Neurology Department due to drug-resistant epilepsy.
Signs of increased intracranial pressure led to ventriculoperitoneal shunt implantation.
MRI of the brain performed after neurosurgery revealed decreased T1 and increased T2 white matter signals in both hemispheres with frontal domination
During hospitalization, massive fluctuations in sodium concentrations were observed (the lowest values of 113 mmol/L)
The patient died at the age of 4 months.

phenotype_specificity.statement: Proband: neonatal-onset course with macrocephaly/hydrocephalus and refractory seizures, which the authors describe as the obligatory features of the neonatal form; a 49-gene epilepsy panel was normal and metabolic causes were excluded; exome sequencing was then done. The authors note hyponatremia is not a typical feature. The paper does not say whether exome analysis found any other candidate variant.

quotes.quote: As presented in our patient, for the neonatal form, two predominant features are obligatory: macrocephaly/hydrocephalus with raised intracranial pressure and often drug-resistant seizures.
The NGS panel of EIEE revealed no abnormalities.
During the diagnostic process, GLUT-1 deficiency, lysosomal storage disorders, organic acidurias, and fatty acid oxidation defects were excluded.
Our patient presented with chronic hyponatremia, which is not a typical feature for AxD.

segregation.statement: Proband's healthy parents and healthy sister were tested by amplicon deep sequencing and did not carry the variant (3 unaffected relatives, all non-carriers). No affected relatives; family history unremarkable.

quotes.quote: We studied the proband’s sample, along with his healthy parents and sister, using ADS with a Nextera XT Kit
The studied variant was excluded in the proband’s parents and sister, suggesting it was caused by a de novo event (germinal mosaicism cannot be excluded).
The patient’s family history was unremarkable.

de_novo.statement: Both parents tested (amplicon deep sequencing) and the variant was absent; the authors call it de novo with germline mosaicism not excluded. Confirmation of parentage is not reported.

quotes.quote: The studied variant was excluded in the proband’s parents and sister, suggesting it was caused by a de novo event (germinal mosaicism cannot be excluded).

variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Missense, p.(Thr396Ile). 41443241 places it in the coil 2B region of GFAP. Both papers state a gain-of-function disease mechanism for GFAP.

quotes.quote: GFAP mutation results in gain-of-function mechanisms [1].

computational_predictions.statement: Conserved nucleotide (PhyloP100 7.34); BayesDel_addAF, BayesDel_noAF, FATHMM_MKL and PrimateAI reported as predicting a damaging effect.

quotes.quote: involving the alteration of a conserved nucleotide (PhyloP100 7.34) was identified.
In silico BayesDel_addAF, BayesDel_noAF, FATHMM_MKL, and PrimateAI tools predict a pathogenic outcome for this variant.

population_data_in_papers.statement: Absent from gnomAD v4 (accessed 2024-02-19) and from an in-house database of more than 12,000 Polish exomes.

quotes.quote: The variant was absent in the gnomAD control database (v4; https://gnomad.broadinstitute.org, accessed on 19 February 2024) and in the in-house database of > 12,000 WES of Polish individuals.

authors_classification.statement: Paprocka et al. classify it as likely pathogenic (PS2 strong, PM1 moderate, PM2 supporting) and say the earlier case suggests a deleterious effect. 41443241 gives no classification for this variant.

quotes.quote: According to the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG), the variant was predicted as “likely pathogenic” (strong, PS2 strong, PM1 moderate, PM2 supporting).
suggesting a deleterious effect of the c.1187C>T variant

concerns: Same-person duplicates: AXD-ID0449 (41443241 Table 3, column 'Paprocka et al', reference 2 = PMID 38540409) is the AXD-ID0214 proband, and AXD-ID0450 (column 'Mura et al', reference 8 = PMID 34865968) is the AXD-ID0430 earlier patient. The four identities are most likely two people.

The Mura et al. patient (AXD-ID0430/AXD-ID0450) appears only in summary sentences and a review table; the original report (PMID 34865968) is not in the batch, and no zygosity, sex or parental testing is given for that person.
Contradiction between papers on the Mura et al. patient: 38540409 says death within the eighth month of life, while 41443241 Table 3 gives 'Within the second year'.
Germline mosaicism in a parent is not excluded (authors' own caveat); parentage confirmation not reported.
The authors' list of ACMG criteria in 38540409 begins with a stray word ('strong,') before the first code; quoted as written under authors_classification.
notes_for_panel: Two distinct people are likely: one de novo proband with full case description (38540409) and one earlier published patient (Mura et al. 2021, not in the batch) seen only second-hand. 41443241 adds no new carrier.
